capabilities.architectureNotes: Foundation of IaaS. All three providers offer comparable general-purpose and memory-optimized shapes. Hybrid extension (Outposts, Arc, Distributed Cloud) differentiates at enterprise scale. Graviton4 (AWS), Ampere Altra (Azure), and Tau T2D (GCP) arm-based instances offer cost/performance advantages.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Patching overhead scales with fleet size. Reserved/committed pricing requires capacity planning discipline. Sole-tenant/dedicated options incur significant premium. Image management (AMI, Gallery, custom images) needs lifecycle governance.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS Lambda has the largest ecosystem and most mature tooling. Azure Durable Functions provides strong stateful workflow support. GCP Cloud Run offers container-native serverless with stronger portability than Lambda. All three scale to zero and support event-driven patterns.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Cold start latency is a concern for latency-sensitive workloads — Provisioned Concurrency (AWS) and always-on plans (Azure) address this at cost. Debugging distributed serverless functions requires mature observability. Cost can surprise at high invocation volume without concurrency controls.

capabilities.architectureNotes: GKE is widely considered the most mature managed Kubernetes offering given Google's authorship of the platform. AKS has strong Azure ecosystem integration and free control plane. EKS has the broadest enterprise adoption in AWS environments. All three support hybrid extension via Anthos, Arc, and EKS Anywhere respectively.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Kubernetes carries significant operational burden even in managed form. Dedicated platform engineering is recommended at enterprise scale. Networking complexity (CNI, service mesh, ingress) is a common friction point. Node autoscaling (Karpenter, KEDA) is essential for cost control.

capabilities.architectureNotes: IAM is the architectural foundation everything else depends on. Azure Entra ID is tightly coupled to the Microsoft ecosystem and assumed by most Azure services. AWS IAM offers the most granular policy model (SCPs, permission boundaries, resource control policies). GCP IAM integrates with Google Workspace identity. All three support PIV/CAC for government.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Misconfigured IAM is the most common enterprise cloud security failure mode. Principle of least privilege must be enforced from day one — retrofitting is painful. Just-In-Time access (PIM in Azure, temporary credentials in AWS) is critical for privileged operations. Service account sprawl is a common governance gap.

capabilities.architectureNotes: All three providers offer comparable VPC/VNet primitives. Differentiation is at the edge: AWS CloudFront has 600+ POPs and Lambda@Edge for edge compute; Azure Front Door has strong global load balancing with built-in WAF; GCP's global Anycast network provides low-latency routing without explicit region selection. Private connectivity options (Direct Connect, ExpressRoute, Dedicated Interconnect) are comparable at 100 Gbps.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Egress charges from VPC are a major hidden cost — architecture should minimize cross-region and internet-bound traffic. CDN configuration drift is a common security gap. WAF rule management requires dedicated attention; managed rule sets reduce overhead but may block legitimate traffic. TIC 3.0 compliance affects federal internet egress architecture.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS S3 is the de facto standard with the widest ecosystem integration. Azure Blob has strong Microsoft data platform integration (Synapse, Fabric, Azure ML). GCS excels with BigQuery native integration. Egress costs are a significant architectural consideration at scale — design to minimize cross-region and internet-bound traffic.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Lifecycle policies are essential for cost control across hot/warm/cold/archive tiers. Object Lock / WORM is important for compliance retention. Bucket-level public access should be denied by default at the organization policy level. Macie (AWS) / Defender for Storage (Azure) / DLP policies (GCP) provide PII detection.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Aurora (AWS) leads on performance/cost for MySQL/PostgreSQL workloads. Azure SQL has the strongest SQL Server compatibility and enterprise licensing path (Hybrid Benefit). Cloud Spanner (GCP) is unique for globally consistent ACID at scale but with significant proprietary lock-in. AlloyDB (GCP) is a strong PostgreSQL-compatible alternative.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Multi-region HA adds cost and complexity. Read replicas do not provide write HA. RDS Custom (AWS) and Managed Instance (Azure) support Oracle/SQL Server lift-and-shift. Cloud Spanner pricing model (nodes + processing units) requires careful capacity planning — cost surprises are common.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS offers the most fragmented but flexible messaging layer (SQS, SNS, Kinesis, MSK, EventBridge each solve distinct problems). Azure Event Hubs has deep Kafka compatibility and strong integration with Synapse and Stream Analytics. GCP Pub/Sub is the simplest operational model but requires Dataflow for complex stream processing. All three support event-driven architecture patterns.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Message ordering guarantees differ: SQS FIFO, Kafka (MSK/Event Hubs), and Pub/Sub ordered delivery have different semantics and cost profiles. At-least-once vs exactly-once delivery affects application design. Retention periods and replay capability are important for audit and reprocessing scenarios.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS Transfer Family is the only native cloud MFT service among the three (SFTP, FTPS, AS2, FTP). GCP and Azure lack native MFT — both rely on partner solutions (GoAnywhere, Axway, MuleSoft). For API management, Apigee (GCP) is the most full-featured lifecycle platform; Azure APIM is deeply integrated with the Microsoft enterprise stack; AWS API Gateway is simpler and cost-effective for basic use cases.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: MFT solutions frequently handle regulated data (CJIS, HIPAA, PII). AS2 for EDI, SFTP for legacy agency integrations, and HTTPS for modern APIs are common in government. Protocol breadth and immutable audit logging are critical compliance differentiators. GoAnywhere, MuleSoft, and Axway can bridge all three cloud environments.

capabilities.architectureNotes: All three providers offer comprehensive compliance program coverage (FedRAMP, CJIS, HIPAA, NIST 800-53, FIPS 140-2/3) at enterprise and government tiers. Azure Government is the most mature for DoD IL4/IL5/IL6. AWS GovCloud has the deepest ITAR/CJIS coverage and broadest DoD IL range. GCP Assured Workloads provides strong commercial compliance controls with growing gov coverage.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Compliance posture requires active management — certification does not mean you are compliant, only that the platform can support compliance. CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) is a frequent requirement for regulated data. Access Transparency and operator access logging are important for government and regulated enterprise. FedRAMP authorization applies to the provider's infrastructure, not your workload.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS CloudWatch is the most widely deployed but has historically felt fragmented (separate metrics, logs, traces, dashboards). Azure Monitor with Application Insights is the most integrated observability platform for Microsoft-stack applications. GCP Cloud Operations (formerly Stackdriver) integrates natively with GKE and Cloud Run. All three now offer managed Prometheus and Grafana to reduce vendor lock-in.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Log ingestion costs scale rapidly — set retention policies and sampling rates early. Distributed tracing across microservices requires instrumentation discipline. SIEM integration (Sentinel, Chronicle, Security Lake) for security observability requires separate configuration from operational monitoring. Custom dashboards are not portable between providers.

capabilities.architectureNotes: BigQuery (GCP) offers the best serverless analytics experience and tightest ML/AI integration. Redshift (AWS) is deeply embedded in the AWS data ecosystem with strong RA3 node performance. Azure Synapse and Microsoft Fabric provide the best integration with Power BI, Microsoft 365, and enterprise data estates. Fabric (Azure) is the most significant recent platform change in this space.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: On-demand query cost models can surprise without governance guardrails — slot/reservation pricing requires capacity planning. Data egress for cross-cloud or on-prem movement adds cost. Schema-on-read (BigQuery, Redshift Spectrum) vs schema-on-write has significant operational implications. Purview (Azure), Dataplex (GCP), and Lake Formation (AWS) provide data governance layers.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Azure OpenAI has the strongest enterprise/gov deployment story for GPT models via the Microsoft partnership. AWS Bedrock provides the widest multi-model choice (Claude, Llama, Mistral, Titan, Nova) without model lock-in — a significant architectural differentiator. GCP Vertex AI GenAI is tightly integrated with Google's data/analytics stack. Government availability is the most active area of parity lag across all three.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Token costs scale rapidly with usage volume. Prompt engineering and RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) are operationally non-trivial. Data residency and model data retention policies differ significantly and require legal review for regulated workloads. Content filtering and guardrails are required before enterprise deployment. Model deprecation cycles are short — pin model versions in production.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Azure DevOps + GitHub (both Microsoft) provide the most integrated enterprise CI/CD ecosystem and the broadest government deployment story. AWS CodePipeline is native to AWS but CodeCommit is no longer accepting new customers (July 2024). GCP Cloud Build is solid but less feature-rich — many GCP shops use GitHub Actions or GitLab CI externally.

STIG-hardened build environments are required for government IL2/IL4. DISA STIG-compliant pipeline patterns are available for all three providers. AWS CodeCommit deprecation requires migration planning for existing CI/CD investments.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS GovCloud has the deepest DoD IL coverage (IL2–IL5) and the strongest ITAR/CJIS track record. Azure Government is the most mature for DoD IL5/IL6 and the only provider with a commercially-available IL6 offering (Azure Govt Secret). GCP Assured Workloads applies compliance controls to standard regions rather than separate cloud partitions — a meaningful architectural difference. For classified workloads above IL5, Azure Govt Secret and AWS C2S/SC2S are the primary options.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: GovCloud and government regions have feature lag compared to commercial — new services and capabilities arrive later and sometimes never. Architect for the lowest common denominator of features available in the target compliance tier. Some services (newer AI models, preview features) may be unavailable in government regions for extended periods. Data sovereignty requirements may mandate specific region selection even within the government cloud.

capabilities.architectureNotes: Azure Arc is the most mature hybrid platform — it extends Azure management, Policy, GitOps, and Defender to any infrastructure including AWS, GCP, and bare metal. AWS Outposts brings native AWS services on-premises with full hardware delivery. GCP Distributed Cloud offers both connected and air-gapped (SCIF-capable) edge hardware. All three support Kubernetes at the edge as the common orchestration layer.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Hybrid architectures introduce network latency, split management plane complexity, and data sovereignty considerations. Hardware refresh cycles for Outposts and Distributed Cloud are provider-managed but require physical facility planning. Arc's agentless approach has lower operational overhead than Outposts/Distributed Cloud hardware. Connectivity reliability to cloud control plane affects on-prem service continuity.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS has the most mature FinOps tooling ecosystem (Cost Explorer, Budgets, Savings Plans, Compute Optimizer, Cost Anomaly Detection). Azure Cost Management is tightly integrated with EA/MCA agreements and Power BI. GCP Billing and Recommender API provide strong programmatic cost optimization. All three support committed use pricing that requires multi-year capacity planning discipline.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Without active governance, cloud costs grow unconstrained. Tagging strategy must be established from day one — retrofitting is extremely difficult. Budget alerts alone are insufficient — anomaly detection and automated remediation are needed at enterprise scale. FinOps as a practice (Cloud Financial Management) requires dedicated cross-functional ownership, not just IT tracking.

capabilities.architectureNotes: AWS Migration Hub + Application Migration Service (MGN) is the most comprehensive lift-and-shift tooling for VM migration. Azure Migrate has the strongest SQL Server and Windows workload migration story with Hybrid Benefit licensing. GCP RAMP (Rapid Assessment & Migration Program) provides structured consulting-led migration. Snowball Edge (AWS) is the leading solution for large-scale offline data migration including Secret-level classified data.
capabilities.operationalConsiderations: Migration projects consistently take longer and cost more than estimated. Rehost (lift and shift) moves risk intact — plan for a modernization phase post-migration. Database migrations are the highest-risk component. Network bandwidth for data transfer must be assessed early. Agent-based migration (MGN, Azure Migrate) requires firewall exceptions that can be difficult in regulated environments.
